content.jointProblem: What mechanisms cause cracking at AutomVoj’s painted mild-steel conveyor-frame welds after prolonged operation at 2–6 °C, and could changes to welding procedure, filler material or joint geometry reduce the damage? The first experiment would compare representative production joints under measured service-relevant cyclic loading at room temperature and chilled conditions, with condensation controlled where feasible, testing whether the researcher’s thermo-mechanical fatigue methods transfer to these frames rather than assuming a low-temperature failure mechanism.

rationale.text: Erić has experimentally investigated the interaction of mechanical fatigue and thermal cycling in welded structural steel, directly relevant to testing the company’s suspected combined-loading mechanism.

sources.quote: Four loading programmes were applied: isothermal fatigue at 20 °C, isothermal fatigue at −30 °C, in-phase thermo-mechanical fatigue (TMF), and out-of-phase TMF, with twelve specimens per programme.

rationale.text: He has experience translating field measurements into fatigue loading spectra, which could help replace the company’s room-temperature workshop test with a service-informed investigation.

sources.quote: Rainflow-counted stress spectra and simultaneous temperature records were used to construct a combined loading environment for assessment.

rationale.text: His residual-stress measurements and cyclic-plasticity modelling provide relevant methods for investigating whether weld stresses contribute to crack development.

sources.quote: A cyclic plasticity FE model employing a Chaboche kinematic hardening rule reproduced the surface relaxation trend within 12% across all conditions.

rationale.text: His group routinely uses fatigue-testing equipment, a climate chamber and fracture-mechanics models, providing a relevant experimental and computational starting point.

sources.quote: The group routinely uses servo-hydraulic fatigue testing machines, a climate chamber capable of reaching −60 °C, and in-house FE models

rationale.text: A joint project matches his explicitly stated interest in combined-loading and low-temperature fatigue investigations.

sources.quote: joint projects involving fatigue testing under low-temperature or combined loading conditions

constraints.text: Tests must represent the actual mild-steel hollow-section construction, protective paint and crossmember-to-stringer joints; generic welded coupons alone would not establish the frame failure mechanism.

sources.quote: Our conveyor frames are welded from mild steel hollow section and painted for corrosion resistance before delivery.
we are seeing weld joint cracking at the main crossmember-to-stringer connections after about 18 months of continuous use.

constraints.text: The experimental design must include the actual chilled operating range and distinguish the unverified effects of thermal cycling, condensation and vibration rather than treating them as established causes.

sources.quote: Our suspicion is that the combination of thermal cycling, condensation, and the vibration load from loaded belts is doing something

constraints.text: The investigation must make an agreed evidence-preservation and sampling plan for the two retained failed sections and available site records before destructive testing.

sources.quote: We have photos and measurements of the cracked joints from site visits, and we still have two of the failed sections in storage.

constraints.text: Combined chilled cyclic-loading tests require external laboratory provision and advance equipment booking; the company lacks this capability and the researcher’s chamber and fatigue machine are shared.

sources.quote: We do not currently have the equipment or know-how to test at low temperatures under cyclic load.
Erić's climate chamber and servo-hydraulic machine are shared with two other research groups; scheduling access for extended test campaigns requires advance coordination.

constraints.text: Company engineering effort must be explicitly allocated around live projects rather than assuming a dedicated R&D team.

sources.quote: We have no dedicated R&D department
our chief engineer and two senior automation engineers who allocate time between live projects and improvement work.

risks: Transfer is unvalidated: the cited thermo-mechanical fatigue experiments used structural-steel plate joints and substantially colder cycles, not painted conveyor hollow sections at 2–6 °C. The initial room-temperature versus chilled comparison must test this transfer using representative joints and service-derived loads.

Condensation-assisted damage and coating effects are not demonstrated in the supplied researcher evidence. If failure inspection indicates a corrosion-driven mechanism, additional corrosion or coating expertise and humidity-control capability may be needed.

The two retained failed sections may not establish how cracks initiated or represent all 14 replacements. An accelerated test could reproduce cracking through a different mechanism unless fracture features and crack locations are compared with field failures.
Researcher availability, laboratory booking dates, project budget, company staff commitment and the required decision deadline remain unknown; these could prevent an adequate test campaign.
The chamber’s minimum temperature does not establish that it can accommodate the required joint fixture or control condensation during cyclic loading. Equipment compatibility remains unconfirmed.
questions: What are the steel grade, hollow-section dimensions, filler designation, welding procedure, production inspection records and coating specification, and do the failed assemblies share a production batch or weld detail?

Can the failed sections and site records be released for examination, and what destructive sampling is permitted? Are unfailed service-aged frames and newly manufactured matching joints available as controls?
Can customer sites provide access for strain, vibration, temperature and humidity measurements, including starts, stops, defrost or wash cycles, payload changes and support conditions?
Can the shared chamber and fatigue machine reproduce the measured loading and 2–6 °C environment with suitable fixtures and controlled condensation, and when can they be booked?
What time can Erić and the company engineers commit, and what budget and decision deadline are available for field measurements, failure analysis, specimens and repeated tests?
Which production changes are feasible, and what evidence, acceptance criteria and applicable customer or structural requirements must be satisfied before a revised weld or joint is released?
